stories.title: 30-Year Treasury Yield Tops 5.33%, a New 19-Year High
stories.summary: The 30-year Treasury yield rose above 5.33% on Tuesday, its highest level in 19 years. CNBC tied the move to worries about inflation and government spending. The rise adds to a broader climb in long-term borrowing costs this week.
stories.whyItMatters: Higher long-term yields raise borrowing costs across the economy, from mortgages to corporate debt, and often pressure stock valuations.
whatToWatch: Whether the 30-year yield holds above 5.33% or pulls back
Fresh inflation or spending data that could add to the pressure
questions: What specific inflation or spending news triggered the latest move?
How high can yields go before they hit stocks or housing hard?

stories.title: U.S. Government Debt Yields Surge at an Awkward Moment
stories.summary: CNBC reports that U.S. government bond yields are climbing sharply, at a time it calls badly timed. A related MarketWatch report points to cheap hedges investors can buy to guard against a stock-market selloff. Together, the stories point to rising anxiety about what higher yields mean for stocks.
stories.whyItMatters: Sharp yield spikes can unsettle equity markets and raise financing costs for the government, companies, and consumers alike.
whatToWatch: Further yield moves and any policy response
Investor demand for hedges against a stock selloff
questions: What makes this timing especially bad, according to CNBC?
Are investors already buying hedges, or just discussing them?

stories.whyItMatters: Gold's pullback shows how the sharp rise in Treasury yields is reshaping demand across asset classes, not just stocks and bonds.
